A satisfying assignment exists. For example, set **p30 = true**. Then every clause of the form “p30 is false or …” is automatically satisfied by p30 being true, and the clause “p24 is false or p29 is true or p30 is true” is also satisfied.

Now choose values to satisfy the remaining clauses, e.g.:
- p2 = true (satisfies “p2 is true or p30 is true”, and many others)
- p9 = false and p20 = false (then “p9 is false or p20 is true” holds)
- p14 = true (then “p13 is false or p14 is true” holds, and many others)
- p5 = true (then “p5 is true or p8 is true” holds)
- p1 = true, p4 = false, p24 = false (then “p1 is true or p4 is true or p24 is true” holds)
- p16 = false, p15 = false, p17 = false, p18 = false, p19 = false, p21 = false, p22 = false, p23 = false, p25 = false, p26 = false, p27 = false, p28 = false, p29 = false
- p3 = true, p10 = true, p11 = true, p12 = true, p13 = true, p6 = true, p7 = true, p8 = true

With these choices, every clause has at least one true literal, so the CNF is satisfiable.
